intro: Many families in Illinois keep festivals that are thousands of years old. They sweep ancestors' graves in spring. They share mooncakes under the fall moon. They cheer for lion dancers in Chicago's Chinatown at Lunar New Year.

In this unit you will learn how these festivals work and where they come from. You will see how Confucius's teaching about family shows up in them. You will visit temples, learn about old exams, and walk through Chinatown.

By the end, you will be able to name the main festivals and explain what families do. You will be able to tell how people of many traditions keep them. And you will know how to visit a temple or festival with respect.
bigQuestion: How do festivals, temples and neighborhoods keep old teachings part of everyday life?

Lunar New Year and the Chinatown parade; Lantern Festival 15 days later
Dragon Boat Festival on the fifth day of the fifth month
Mid-Autumn Festival; Teachers' Day in Taiwan on September 28

test.q: What does a lunar calendar count by?
test.why: A lunar calendar counts months by the moon's changes.

test.q: Which animal starts the twelve-year zodiac cycle?
test.why: The cycle begins with the Rat and ends with the Pig.

test.q: What ends the Lunar New Year season?
test.why: The Lantern Festival on the first full moon ends about fifteen days of New Year.

test.q: On Qingming, what do families do?
test.why: Qingming is Tomb-Sweeping Day, when families care for ancestors' graves.

test.q: Confucius's teaching of xiao is about what?
choices: Respect and care for parents and family
test.why: Xiao is respect and care for parents, in life and after death (Analects 2.5).

test.q: The Dragon Boat Festival remembers which poet?
test.why: People tell that the festival remembers the poet Qu Yuan.

test.q: Who is the lady in the moon in the Mid-Autumn legend?
test.why: Chang'e floated to the moon in the legend told at Mid-Autumn.

test.q: What is Lunar New Year called in Korea?
test.why: Koreans call Lunar New Year Seollal.
The largest Temple of Confucius is in Qufu, his hometown.

test.q: Why is Teachers' Day in Taiwan held on September 28?
choices: It is the Mid-Autumn full moon
test.why: Taiwan honors teachers on Confucius's traditional birthday.

test.q: What happens in a Daoist temple?
choices: Visitors light incense and priests lead ceremonies
test.why: Daoist temples are living places of incense, chanting and ceremonies.

test.q: About how long did China's civil-service exams last?
test.why: The exams ran from about 605 to 1905 CE, about 1,300 years.

test.q: Where does Chicago's Lunar New Year parade go?

test.why: The three teachings are Confucian, Daoist and Buddhist traditions, often drawn on together.

test.q: Which is the most respectful choice at a temple?
choices: Speak softly and ask before photos
test.why: Quiet voices and asking first show respect in a place of worship.

write.prompt: How do festivals show respect for family? Choose two festivals from this unit. For each, tell what families do. Then use Analects 2.5 (retold from Legge's translation) to explain how some families connect it to Confucius's teaching of xiao.
tips: Name each festival and when it happens.
Name the book you cite, like Analects 2.5.
Say who believes or does something: "Many families..." or "Confucius taught..."
Use at least two unit words, like ancestors or xiao.
